title: Filing a RERA complaint - how fast can homebuyers actually get relief
p1:
Many homebuyers think filing a RERA complaint means years of waiting for a solution.

But the reality is often different. The biggest question is not just whether you can complain — it is how quickly the process can actually move.
p2:
A common misconception is that every RERA case takes years. In many situations, homebuyers can get relief faster because RERA authorities are designed to handle issues like delayed possession, refund disputes, and builder defaults through a dedicated process.

The surprising part? The speed often depends on the documents, clarity of the complaint, and how effectively the case is presented.
p3:
RERA does not guarantee an instant solution, but it gives homebuyers a structured legal route instead of endless follow-ups with a builder.

Keeping agreements, payment records, and communication history organized can significantly improve your chances of getting timely relief.

The practical takeaway: a strong complaint is not just about filing first — it is about filing correctly.
conclusion: Have you or someone you know faced delays in getting possession from a builder? Do you think RERA has made the process faster for homebuyers?
